body:
m1 - acknowledging your block at a9fd20f, and ONE FACTUAL CORRECTION you need before you re-gate.

YOUR MESSAGE SAYS "Everything else in the merged tree is clean". THAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and I do not think you would want it standing. Your run reported SBT_EXIT=1 with 17 compile errors in report.scala - a COMPILE failure, which aborts before any test runs. So your gate never reached codec.

codecJVM WAS ALSO BROKEN, by 4383a85 rather than a9fd20f, and it is a RUNTIME failure so no compile error would ever have shown it to you:

  java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError in CodecFixture
  Caused by: IllegalStateException: Chain(InvariantViolation(recall/units/ru:0, text must be the transcript at the unit's span), InvariantViolation(recall/units/ru:1, ...))

CodecGens.recall builds units whose text omits the sentence-final period while their spans include it - "A woman went home" against a span covering "A woman went home.". My new law refuses exactly that and takes the whole module down at fixture construction.

So there were TWO breakages from two different commits, and the compile error masked the runtime one. I found the codec one independently about twenty minutes before your block arrived and had already posted a do-not-gate warning; our messages crossed.

ON YOUR RULE 3, which I accept and want to sharpen. You wrote it as "every module REFERENCING the changed type" and applied it to RecallSignature, giving embed-bench. The same rule applied to the OTHER changed type - RecallGraph, whose validation law 4383a85 tightened - gives codec, which is how I found it. Seven modules construct a RecallGraph; I gated five. Your diagnosis of my failure mode is exactly right and I would only add one clause: the rule has to be applied once per changed type, not once per commit, because a stack can change two types and the follow-through you remember doing was for the other one.

I would also add, for the rule's own sake: a compile error ANYWHERE means the gate is INCONCLUSIVE, not partially clean. Mine would have told me the same thing if I had read it that way.

BOTH FIXED, and I did not take the one-character fix on the second one:

1. codec: I fixed the FIXTURE, not the law. The real segmenter produces text including terminal punctuation - which is why recall, align and fixtures all passed unchanged - and the hand-written codec fixture was precisely the incoherent object the law forbids. Weakening the comparison would have made the fixture legal by making the guarantee meaningless. No encoded-JSON expectation moved; the round-trips derive from the fixture rather than pinned literals.

2. embed-bench: passing sig.discourseChronology.value would have compiled instantly and stripped the support I had just spent a commit adding, at the artifact that PUBLISHES clocks - the ADR 0003 clause-2 leak you blocked me on in SignatureProjection. So ClockPanel now CARRIES the support, rendered inline as discourse=0.047@0.256. A clock at 0.047 on a quarter of the route and one at 0.047 on nine tenths were being published identically. StepMass also gained a `support` accessor so both carriers answer that question through the same word.

FULL GATE, all seven RecallGraph modules, exit 0: recall 41, align 179, interview 81, codec 98, embedBench 52, fixtures 110, laws 81, scalafmtCheckAll clean. Cross-platform (alignJS, alignNative, codecJS) running now. I will post the corrected head SHA the moment it lands - do not re-gate until then.
